title: Set a probe positioner on a probe station: slide it to the die, hold it as its magnet locks, trim its tip by knob
instruction: Set the loose probe positioner up on the marked die. Its magnet is off. Slide it along the platen until its needle points at the die with the tip near the mark, never touching the other needle, the wafer or the microscope. Keep it from shifting while you push its magnet lever to ON. Then turn its X and Y knobs to bring the tip over the mark, short of the other probe's tip. Let go.
context: Probing a chip on a manual probe station starts by setting each probe positioner round the die. It stands on the steel platen on a switchable magnet: with the lever off it is slid until its needle is over the die, the lever is thrown to clamp it (MPI TS150 manual: 'The side "ON", "OFF" lever is used to toggle the magnetic clamping'), and the tip is then brought to its place with the positioner's micrometer knobs, tips '2-3 mm apart' before landing (MIT MTL IV-probe SOP). The tip is 14.4 cm from the base's centre, so a degree of twist moves it 2.5 mm; throwing the lever drags a free base unless it is held; each knob turn moves the tip 0.3 mm, with the other needle 2 mm beyond the mark. The task ends before the tips land.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y left; heights above the bench top. (1) Platen: nickel-plated steel 33.2 cm along x by 23.5 cm along y, 1.2 cm thick, its top 12 cm up, centred at (42, 0), with a 25 cm round opening over the chuck (MPI TS150 datasheet: about 330 x 235 mm, R125 opening), so steel remains at its near end (x 25.4 to 29.5 on the centre line, wider at the corners) and far end. Chuck 16 cm across, its top 28 mm below the platen top (datasheet minimum), with a 150 mm wafer 0.7 mm thick; the die is marked at its centre (42, 0) with a 1 mm cross. Microscope: a bridge across y at x 42 on posts at y +/-20, its lens (4.4 cm across) about 4 cm above the wafer, set so the frame is about 12 mm wide. (2) Positioner 1 is clamped on the far end, its base centred at (56.6, 0), needle pointing -x, tip 2 mm past the mark at (42.2, 0), 1 mm above the wafer. (3) Positioner 2 stands loose on the near end at (27.6, 6.5), lever OFF, needle pointing +x, tip 1 mm above the wafer at (42, 6.5), its X and Y stages centred. Both are MP40-class: base 65 mm along y by 40 mm along x (listing: 65 x 40 mm, 13 mm XYZ travel, magnetic mount), 100 mm tall, 0.6 kg; arm and 0.51 mm tungsten needle (0.020 in tip stock) reach 14.4 cm forward of the base's centre, the arm 4 cm above the platen and the needle sloping down to the tip (sizes, mass: estimates). Base on platen: friction 0.3 with the lever OFF (estimate; runs pass 0.25 to 0.5; the real trial sets 0.25 to 0.5 by tilt; 4 N only at 0.3 or more); at ON the magnet pulls it down with 343 N (first4magnets 19206: 70 kg, 686 N, pull-off on thick steel, taken at half for the 12.7 mm bar). Magnet lever on the base's +y face: a 3 cm arm hinged 4.5 cm up, standing up at OFF, with a flat 8 x 20 x 16 mm knob 14 mm off the face; it swings forward 70 degrees to its stop and counts as ON past 62 degrees; 3 N at the knob (no maker publishes it; MIL-STD-1472H gives 2.8 to 11 N for a finger push button; the real trial measures it on a force gauge and accepts 2.7 to 4 N, 4 N only at friction 0.3 or more). X knob on the base's rear (-x) face, Y knob on its -y face: each a 16 mm cylinder standing 12 mm out, its axis 6 cm above the platen, 0.3 mm of tip travel per turn (MP40 screw resolution 300 um; estimate), 0.02 N m drag (estimate). Both YAM arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. Real trial (README table, about USD 340 for the rig): two 1/2 x 2 in steel flat bars as the platen's two steel ends on printed risers, a printed 160 mm chuck with a paper die target, a used lever-type switchable-magnet probe positioner (a unit with a detent or turned-handle switch outside the lever window is rejected), a second magnetic base holding the fixed needle, two single 0.52 mm tungsten probes glued into printed arms (tip 14.4 cm ahead of the base's centre), and a 2 MP USB microscope on a bridge, frame about 12 mm wide; a printed 1 mm scale reads the 0.3 mm trim and the tip's shift, two dial indicators (placed after the latch, clear of the knobs) the base's drift, a phone level app its tilt, a multimeter's continuity beep any needle touch, and a phone on a stand over the bench (whole platen and both hands, 30 fps, ruler, sound on) the 3 cm hands-clear and touch calls.
scoring: Read at the end the way a technician reads it: the tip against the mark on the station's microscope camera, through its reticle or scale bar (a person can read 0.3 mm there). 0.25: positioner 2 upright (tilt under 2 degrees), its needle within 5 degrees of the line to the mark, the tip within 4 mm of the mark in plan. 0.5: and the lever ON with the tip within 4 mm of the mark at the latch, the tip moved under 0.5 mm across the throw. 0.75: and the tip within 0.3 mm of the mark after the knobs were turned at least 90 degrees in all since the latch, the base moved under 0.5 mm since the latch. 1.0: and every fingertip 3 cm from positioner 2 and its needle, all still for 1 s, positioner 1 moved under 1 mm. 0: a needle touches the other needle, the wafer or the lens, or a fingertip touches a needle, the wafer or the lens. The contact tests use sim-only margins (a fingertip within 6 mm of a needle or 4 mm of the lens, or low over the wafer; needle centre lines within 0.6 mm; a needle within 0.5 mm of the lens or 0.2 mm of the wafer); on the bench a touch is a continuity beep or one seen on the camera.
reset_notes: Nothing is random: positioner 2 at its mark, lever OFF, knobs at zero. Check each needle for a bent tip before a trial.
fidelity: Positioner 2's base is a free body on the platen (friction 0.3; runs pass 0.25-0.5); X, Y stages follow the knobs (0.3 mm a turn); the magnet is a 343 N pull past 62 degrees (half the 19206's 686 N rating; runs pass 200-686 N). Lever 3 N (no maker figure; MIL-STD-1472H finger band 2.8-11 N; runs pass 2.7-4 N, 5 N fails, rejected on a gauge); swing, drag, masses: estimates. Needle collider 1.2 mm across (real 0.51 mm); needle contact: centre lines under 0.6 mm (sim margin).
